title: Huihui-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B abliterated Q5_K_M on a 64GB Mac — planned dev-agent lane
slug_note: A buying-advice thread distilled into a starting recipe: Q5_K_M (24.7GB) via llama-server --hf-repo with --jinja at 65k context, wired into OpenCode as an OpenAI-compatible provider. No numbers yet — nobody in the thread owns the machine.

variation.quant_detail: Q5_K_M recommended start (24.7GB); abliterated (refusal-removed) distill tuned toward Claude-4.7-Opus-style agent behavior
variation.revision_note: HF snapshot of shennguyen/Huihui-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Claude-4.7-Opus-abliterated-GGUF resolved and served on the Spark during the 2026-11-16 re-run

engine.config: llama-server with Metal (default-on, GPU layers auto), --jinja for the tool/chat template, kept at defaults until the tool loop verifies stable. OpenCode connects through the OpenAI-compatible provider.

requirements.notes: 24.7 GB Q5_K_M weights + KV on unified memory; 32 GB is the working floor for the 64 GB Mac lane, which stays unverified. Measured on a DGX Spark (2026-11-16): 25.7 GB resident on the GPU with -c 65536.

steps.text: Install llama.cpp (see Step 0 in Quick start). On Ubuntu / DGX OS install libssl-dev first, or --hf-repo cannot download.
point OpenCode's OpenAI-compatible provider at the server's host:port (default 127.0.0.1:8080)

measurements.method: openai_bench (SR-344 short_bench.py): streaming /v1/chat/completions, single stream, one warm-up discarded, fresh nonce per summarise prompt (cold prefill), decode = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token time), temperature 0.6, median of 3; summarise neutral filler (633-token prompt, 256 output tokens)

openai_bench (SR-344 short_bench.py): streaming /v1/chat/completions, single stream, one warm-up discarded, fresh nonce per summarise prompt (cold prefill), decode = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token time), temperature 0.6, median of 3; write an LRU cache module with tests (37-token prompt, 512 output tokens)

openai_bench (SR-344 short_bench.py): streaming /v1/chat/completions, single stream, one warm-up discarded, fresh nonce per summarise prompt (cold prefill), decode = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token time), temperature 0.6, median of 3; write a 400-word essay (31-token prompt, 512 output tokens)

openai_bench (SR-344 short_bench.py): streaming /v1/chat/completions, single stream, one warm-up discarded, fresh nonce per summarise prompt (cold prefill), decode = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token time), temperature 0.6, median of 3; time to first streamed token on the ~630-token summarise prompt
nvidia-smi per-process GPU allocation for the cell's own llama-server during the bench (weights + KV at -c 65536); llama.cpp build 12035 (commit 4e910a86e)

caveats: FIXED (negative result kept, law 3): the recipe as published in the thread was broken — two DGX Spark runs (2026-10-26, llama.cpp build 11866; 2026-11-02, build 12035) passed the literal placeholder `--hf-file <q5_k_m.gguf>`, so llama-server had no real file to fetch and exited before downloading anything. On 2026-11-16 we re-ran it on the Spark with the repo's actual file name (the command now recorded in Run): server ready after 2094 s — that time is the 24.7 GB download, llama.cpp needs ~6 s to load once the file is local — the functional check passed, and the box measurements below are from that run.
Original thread advice (unverified, kept per law 1): the OP hasn't bought the machine and the replier owns no Apple hardware — 'expect tens of tokens/sec' was an explicit guess and is not captured.
The only actual in-thread run used MLX on Apple Silicon (different engine) — noted as the alternative lane.
abliterated checkpoint: refusal behavior removed; verify tool-call reliability before agent use.
shennguyen is not on the law-11 quant whitelist — lane kept as a measured Spark run, not a matrix entry.
